execution_description: Separate Claude subagent context in a cloud Claude Code session; same model family as the designer; not an independent human or vendor.

findings.claim: The twist check and its 0.05 mm criterion are not justified, and on the real face geometry the declared case fails the designer's own relaxed criterion. (a) The "abuse case" load is 3 N, which equals force_band_max_n, the top of the normal press band. Its 4 mm offset lies inside the face rather than at its edge: the window spans z 10-18 and the leaf centreline is at z 12.5, so the top edge is 5.5 mm off the leaf axis. A normal-magnitude press on the upper part of the face is therefore labelled abuse. (b) With the 0.15 mm criterion used for normal presses, both twist checks fail (0.1404 and 0.0993 mm). The change to 0.05 mm has no stated basis, such as a tolerance stack or the consequence of contact. It is also smaller than the print accuracy the contract itself lists as unqualified for the 0.4 mm gaps. This is a threshold lowered until the check passes, which project rules forbid. (c) A 3 N press at the real top edge gives 16.5 N·mm, i.e. 1.76 deg by the recipe's own beam_twist_deg (twist scales linearly with torque). At that angle my read-only probe of the exported STEPs measured 0.043 mm to the shell with the button at rest pose, which is below 0.05 mm, and 0.058-0.071 mm when combined with press rotation. The opposite sign (-1.76 deg) reaches 0.000 mm. (d) The plan says "normal presses keep 0.15 mm", but no check combines press rotation with the twist that any off-axis press produces. The face centroid (z about 14) is itself 1.5 mm off the leaf axis. My probe found 0.29-0.31 mm for a 3 N centroid press combined with full press, so the statement is plausible, but it is unverified in the record.
evidence: recipe design_parameters: edge_press_force_n 3.0, edge_press_offset_mm 4.0, force_band_max_n 3.0, window_z_min/max 10/18, leaf_z_min/max 6.5/18.5 (leaf axis z 12.5), twist_min_gap_mm 0.05
measurements.json twist-positive-clear end distance 0.1404 mm; twist-negative-clear 0.0993 mm, continuous_distance_lower_bound 0.0179 mm, continuous_swept_motion not_proven, yet verdict pass
verification_plan: "Twist (abuse case, ASSUMED 3 N at the face edge) ... stays at least 0.05 mm (normal presses keep 0.15 mm)"

Read-only CadQuery probe on button+actuator_insert vs shell STEP: twist +1.759 deg -> 0.0434 mm; -1.759 deg -> 0.0 mm; press -1.07/-2.14 deg + twist +1.759 -> 0.0576/0.0708 mm; twist +/-1.279 reproduces 0.1404/0.0993 mm
Task note: criterion first drafted at 0.15 mm and set to 0.05 mm by the designer before freezing; AGENTS.md forbids lowering thresholds to pass
unverified_requirements: "print accuracy of the 0.4 mm gaps ... not qualified"
findings.proposed_change: Do not lower the criterion. Either fix the geometry, e.g. put the leaf axis at the face centroid height and/or widen or thicken the leaf so a 3 N press at the real face edge (5.5 mm, or the true worst-case arm) keeps at least 0.15 mm in combined press plus twist poses. Or keep 0.15 mm and report the twist case as a FAIL or open risk to the owner. Derive edge_press_offset_mm from the face geometry instead of a free constant. Drop the "abuse" label unless the load exceeds the normal force band. If a smaller abuse gap is ever wanted, state its basis (load above the normal band, tolerance stack, consequence of contact) in the contract.
findings.required_test: Rebuild and run twist checks at the torque from 3 N at the measured top-edge and bottom-edge arms, both alone and combined with press rotation at 0, mid and deepest angles (with the pivot-play offsets), with at least 0.15 mm required. Add a recorded combined press-plus-twist check for a centroid press. Use enough samples that continuous_swept_motion is not "not_proven".

findings.claim: Revision 14 flagged leaf root stress concentration as blocking. In revision 15 it is addressed only by an ASSUMED Kt of 1.5, while the CAD still has sharp 90-degree re-entrant corners. At the root the 1.6 mm leaf meets the 3.5 mm block flush on its bending faces. At the tip the 12 mm wide leaf joins a pad only 7 mm tall (z 10.5-17.5), leaving a notch. For a zero-radius corner the factor is not bounded by 1.5, so the stress "pass" (11.05 vs 16.7 MPa, limit reached at Kt of about 2.27) rests on an assumption that the geometry does not support. The contract says "a fillet would lower it", but no fillet exists.
evidence: leaf_spring/iso.png and carrier_block/iso.png: no fillets; leaf is a box from x -31 to -9 touching the block (y 16.5-20) and pad (z 10.5-17.5)
measurements.json leaf-spring-beam: nominal 7.36 MPa, peak 11.05 MPa, allowed 16.7 MPa (0.5 x 33.4 MPa tensile), stress_concentration 1.5 ASSUMED
design_basis assumption: "ASSUMED 1.5 at the sharp leaf root and tip corners (no fillet modeled); a fillet would lower it."
findings.proposed_change: Model root and tip fillets (e.g. r >= 1 mm, so a Kt near 1.5 has a stated geometric basis), extend the pad over the full leaf width or taper the joint, and cite the Kt source for the modelled radius. Otherwise state in the contract that the stress check is indeterminate for sharp corners.
findings.required_test: Rebuild with fillets and rerun leaf-spring-beam with Kt from a cited chart for the modelled r/t and step ratio; confirm via the trace that the fillet solids exist in leaf/block/pad.

findings.claim: The explicit intent "もっと押しやすく" is not traced to any recipe function, criterion or reported quantity. Functions F1-F6 cover transmitting force, guiding, mounting, actuating, the rest stop and the shell, but nothing states how this design is easier to press. The CAD's own numbers point the other way and are not surfaced as such. The leaf adds about 1.0 N at the plunger at the latest operating point (0.60 mm of 1.00 mm travel, i.e. 0.6 x 1.71 N) on top of the switch's up to 1.47 N. That makes the click about 2.5 N, versus at most 1.47 N for the bare switch, and 2.65 N at full travel. Without inventing a target, the contract should disclose this so the owner can judge. The only force criterion is the ASSUMED 0.3-3 N band, which says nothing about "easier".
evidence: FLOW_RESULT 1_intent explicit ["もっと押しやすく"], unknown ["target force","travel",...]
recipe functions F1_transmit_force, F2_guide_button, F2_mount, F3_actuate_switch, F5_rest_stop, F6_connect_shell: none addresses ease of pressing
measurements.json leaf-spring-beam force: beam_n 1.714 N at deep travel, switch_operating_max_n 1.471 N, total 2.651 N
FLOW_RESULT 8_recipe switch_profile_fit zippy_df_pin travel_to_operate_max 0.60 mm, travel_to_pin_flush_max 1.00 mm
findings.proposed_change: Add an explicit trace of the intent: state which design feature is meant to make pressing easier (face size or position, travel, force) and report the computed force at the face at the operating point and at full travel, with and without the leaf. Label "easier" as UNKNOWN or owner-defined. Do not invent a numeric target.
findings.required_test: Report the computed face force at the operating point and at the deepest angle for the face centroid and edges (moment balance about the pivot), next to the switch-only force, in the unverified requirements.

findings.claim: The flow record and the recipe do not trace the same functions, and the chosen concept text contradicts revision 15 and the binding owner policy. The decomposition defines F4_restore_button and F5_limit_overtravel ("Motion stops before the switch housing is loaded"). The recipe drops F4 and reuses the F5 prefix for a different function (F5_rest_stop). It also has two F2 ids (F2_guide_button, F2_mount). The chosen candidate (C_flexure, G_leaf, S_switch) still states "A PETG leaf ..." and "Printed in place with the shell" / "Printed in place; no pin or tabs", while revision 15 is ABS only with a separately printed carrier and insert pins. S_switch covers F5_limit_overtravel while saying it "does NOT keep the switch unloaded", so the decomposed behaviour is not met. This is honestly worded there, but it is not carried as an unmet function into the recipe.
evidence: FLOW_RESULT 3_function_decomposition F4_restore_button, F5_limit_overtravel

FLOW_RESULT 5_6 candidate 28716d57...: C_flexure assumption "A PETG leaf inside the static stress allowance...", assembly_method "Printed in place with the shell."; G_leaf "Printed in place; no pin or tabs."
recipe.functions keys: F1_transmit_force, F2_guide_button, F2_mount, F3_actuate_switch, F5_rest_stop, F6_connect_shell
Owner policy (binding): ABS only; recipe material polymaker_polylite_abs
findings.proposed_change: Re-synthesise or annotate the chosen concept for revision 15 (ABS, separate carrier, insert pins). Give the recipe functions ids that map one-to-one to the decomposition (F4 restore via the leaf, F5 limit overtravel marked as not met / switch-bottoming accepted as ASSUMED), and give the rest stop its own new id.
findings.required_test: Check that every decomposition function id appears in the recipe functions or is listed as unmet, and that no concept text in the flow record names PETG or print-in-place for revision 15.

findings.claim: The plan says the press envelope reaches "pin flush for the deepest registered switch", but angles_v15 takes the maximum only over profiles with verdict pass. Only zippy_df_pin passes; omron_d2f_pin, huano_mouse_generic and kailh_gm20 are unverified. The envelope therefore covers one profile, and the wording overstates coverage.
evidence: side_button_leaf_recipe.py angles_v15: max(... for f in fits if f["verdict"] == "pass")
FLOW_RESULT 8_recipe switch_profile_fit: 1 pass, 3 unverified
findings.proposed_change: Reword to "pin flush for zippy_df_pin (the only profile with complete data); other registered profiles unverified".
findings.required_test: Text check of the verification_plan against the switch_profile_fit list.

findings.claim: The stated print assumption is that the carrier is printed with the leaf thickness along the build axis. The block bottom (y 16.5) sits 1.0 mm below the leaf (y 17.5-19.1) and the pad (y >= 17.5). If the block bottom is on the bed, the leaf's lower bending face (the highest-stress surface) is printed on support across its whole 22 x 12 mm. The contract mentions support removal near the leaf only as unqualified, not as a consequence of this geometry.
evidence: carrier_block y 16.5-20; leaf y 17.5-19.1; button ymin 17.5 (probe of exported STEPs)
design_basis: "carrier printed with the leaf thickness along the build axis..."
findings.proposed_change: Make the leaf bottom face coplanar with the block bottom (or state an explicit orientation with the support location) so the leaf bending face is not a support interface. Otherwise state the support-scarred bending face as a known risk.
findings.required_test: Slice or inspect the carrier STEP in the stated orientation and report whether any support touches the leaf bending faces.

findings.claim: rest-gap-insert-to-pin requires 0.049 mm against a 0.05 mm design value. It only confirms the CAD reproduces the parameter. The "no switch force at rest" claim (the revision 14 fix) depends on the insert-length print tolerance and the switch FP tolerance, and neither is analysed. This is not a defect if mis-sizing is benign (the lug still holds the face), but the contract presents the rest-pose fix as a property rather than a nominal value.
evidence: clearance_checks rest-gap-insert-to-pin min_mm 0.049 (= rest_gap_mm - 0.001); measured 0.0500 mm
design_basis: "At rest the actuator does not touch the switch pin (fixed gap), so no switch force pushes the face outward"
findings.proposed_change: State that the fixed gap is nominal. Add that with an insert printed long by more than 0.05 mm the switch preloads the face outward against the lug (the face stays flush, pretravel is shortened), and that a short insert adds dead travel.
findings.required_test: Tolerance note or parametric rebuild with the insert protrusion at +/-0.1 mm, checking that the rest-outward-blocked and press checks still pass.

evidence_inspections.observation: Plain cylinder (recipe: r 1.0 mm, length 5.2 mm, 1.2 mm protrusion for zippy_df_pin); no chamfer or lead-in on either end for the 0.05 mm radial press fit into the 0.95 mm plunger hole.

Closed stand-in shell from outside; the side-button face sits flush in the window and only the 0.4 mm running-gap seam is visible. Carrier, pins, lug and switch are hidden inside, so this image shows the outer-form requirement only, not the mechanism.

subject_digest 391f5a67... and recipe_context_digest f2aa0494... match the packet; it holds the full recipe context (edge_press_offset_mm 4.0, twist_min_gap_mm 0.05, stress_concentration 1.5) and the measurement set; measurements.overall_verdict is "unknown" and geometry_checks_verdict is "pass".

Curved skin piece with the spine, plunger block, tab riser and stop tab behind it and the pad arm on the left. The face is about 8 mm tall (window z 10-18), and its top edge is clearly further from the leaf centreline (z 12.5) than its bottom edge.

Rectangular 5 x 3.5 x 12 mm block with two through clearance holes (r 1.1) for the insert pins. No fillet or transition is visible where the leaf joins it; the leaf is a separate solid that only touches the block face at x = -31.
Plain 22 x 12 x 1.6 mm rectangular plate with sharp edges. No root or tip fillet is modelled, so the stress-concentration factor of 1.5 used in the stress check has no geometric basis in this CAD.

All checks report pass and overall_verdict is "unknown". twist-positive end distance 0.1404 mm and twist-negative 0.0993 mm: both below 0.15 mm and passing only against the 0.05 mm criterion; twist-negative continuous lower bound 0.0179 mm is "not_proven". press-to-deepest min sampled 0.324 mm (with play). Leaf peak stress 11.05 MPa against 16.7 MPa allowed (Kt 1.5 ASSUMED); added leaf force 1.71 N plus 1.47 N for the switch gives 2.65 N total.

Headed insert pin (head r 1.6 x 0.8 mm, shank r 1.0 x 6.5 mm). No lead-in chamfer for the 0.05 mm interference press into the r 0.95 post hole. Printed ABS, consistent with the owner policy (no screw).
Identical to pin_1: a headed printed ABS pin with no lead-in chamfer. It sits 5.5 mm above pin_1 on the same block.

Lug is the stop_lug_box clipped by the cavity loft, so it has a slanted outer face where it meets the inner skin. It is a separate solid in the export but declared as the same print as the shell; at rest it touches the button tab (distance 0.0).

Stand-in loft shell with the side window cut and an open bottom rim. The posts and lug are not visible from this viewpoint. The outer form is otherwise unchanged, which matches the base-shape check (0 of 248 base points off form).
Plain box placeholder, 12.7 x 6.65 x 5.8 mm (zippy_df_pin profile) on the ASSUMED PCB plane. It has no terminals, mounting holes or PCB, so it represents only the switch envelope.
Plain box pin placeholder (1.2 x 0.7 x 2.9 mm; the 1.2 mm x size is UNKNOWN and assumed), modelled at the maximum free position 0.05 mm below the insert tip.

remaining_uncertainties: Revision 14 blockers: the unreacted rest pose looks fixed (fixed gap plus lug, outward rotation blocked at all 9 pivot-play offsets); the print-in-place gaps are removed by the separate carrier; leaf twist and root stress concentration are not adequately fixed (R1, R2).

Owner policy check: every printed part is ABS (polymaker_polylite_abs) and no screws are used (insert pins and actuator insert are printed). Compliant in the recipe, but retention of 0.05 mm-interference printed pins and insert is unqualified and has no lead-in chamfers.
What "easier to press" means (force, travel, face size or position, click feel) is a question only the owner can answer.
Real switch model, PCB plane and shell are not measured; the PCB plane is placed from the design (ASSUMED), so on the real board the insert length is the free variable.

Switch bottoming: no hard stop, and the switch takes thumb overtravel beyond its datasheet overtravel (OT min 0.2 mm, while pin flush needs about 1.0 mm of travel). The maximum allowable force is UNKNOWN and needs a physical test.
Leaf creep, fatigue, layer adhesion and FDM-printed modulus versus datasheet typical values are UNKNOWN; beam theory only.

Press clearance: my 13-sample nominal-axis sweep (0 to -2.139 deg) found a monotonic minimum of 0.372 mm to the shell. This supports the sampled pass, although the recorded continuous bound is "not_proven".
Physical tests still required: press force and click feel with the real switch, face rubbing under edge presses, pin and insert retention, and gap accuracy after printing.
Reviewer independence: same model family as the designer; no physical test or human review was performed.
